     "id": "c3-expr-caps (potentials.py:132, MEDIUM; SEC-L3 residual)",
     "status": "fixed",
     "fix": "_custom_expr never hands the raw string to sympy. Python's ast parses it once (no convert_xor), so '^' stays BitXor and is refused with 'write powers with **'. A strict allow-list covers numbers, names, + - * / **, unary +/-, one-argument sqrt/log/exp/sin/cos/tanh/cosh/sinh, and Rational(int literals). Every node of the unevaluated tree is then bounded before any evaluation: literal |x|<=1e30; every exponent |x|<=64, constant-looking or not; exact digits <=1000; the factor of exp-of-log <=64 (sympy rewrites exp(k*log(x)) as x**k); <=512 nodes; <=32 levels of effective nesting. Symbols count as magnitude 1, so cancellations such as phi-phi+9**9 can't hide a power. Only then is the same tree evaluated with sympy operators, which gives the identical expression (srepr) sympify built for accepted input. Two further bypasses were found and fixed: Rational(9)**(phi-phi+9**9) and exp(9**9*log(9)).",
